overview: Debounce the fetch by an illustrative 200 ms; abort the previous lookup and also compare requestGeneration before committing. A late response for ca must never overwrite cam. Input text remains separate from the committed selection. The graph separates browser interaction state, server query state and the existing backend. It is one defensible approach; equivalent boundaries and well-argued alternatives are welcome.
limitations: Design checks inspect structure and written evidence only; they do not execute a UI or prove accessibility/performance.

estimation.assumption: 10 keystrokes in 1 s; 200 ms quiet-period debounce
estimation.calculation: 10 immediate input updates; often 1 lookup after the burst, but pauses can trigger more
estimation.result: Reduces request bursts without delaying local typing
estimation.implication: Measure input responsiveness and request count under variable latency; debounce is not a correctness mechanism.

components.purpose: Keyboard, pointer, touch and assistive-technology entry point. Client architecture only; backend internals are external dependencies.
components.rationale: Own this responsibility at the Browser / User boundary; keep communication explicit through the diagrammed dependency.

components.purpose: Debounce the fetch by an illustrative 200 ms; abort the previous lookup and also compare requestGeneration before committing. A late response for ca must never overwrite cam. Input text remains separate from the committed selection. Performance plan: Mid-range phone, long-tail latency, at most 10 suggestions mounted; target immediate input feedback before network completion. Accessibility: Use combobox/listbox semantics, labelled input, aria-expanded, aria-controls and aria-activedescendant; Arrow keys move active option, Enter commits, Escape closes. Keep DOM focus in input and announce result count politely. Failure recovery: Ignore obsolete generations even if abort arrived too late; show retry for the current query only and keep typed text. Trade-off: Fetch on each change with request identity for small workloads; debounce saves traffic but delays first suggestions. A headless controlled component supports reuse while a wrapper owns caching.

failureCases.scenario: An older slow request succeeds after a newer fast one
failureCases.handling: Ignore obsolete generations even if abort arrived too late; show retry for the current query only and keep typed text.

failureCases.scenario: Route or identity changes while work is in flight
failureCases.handling: Dispose subscriptions, abort obsolete reads and ignore old generations; partition/clear private cache before showing a new account. Preserve only explicitly safe drafts.
